source_refs.note: Topic 18.5.1 with skin colour, wheat grain colour and the For Information box (PDF 96-98); Figure 18.7 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: Polygenic characters are controlled by many gene pairs, not just one. All the alleles of these genes contribute to the same trait in an additive way, some increasing and some decreasing the effect, and their combined effect produces a single trait. Polygenic traits therefore show a range of differences, continuous variation, in a population.
Examples of polygenic traits are height, skin colour, weight and intelligence in humans, and grain colour in plants.

Skin colour depends on the amount of the pigment melanin: more melanin gives darker skin. About 60 genes are involved, but for understanding three genes, A, B and C, are taken; the alleles A, B and C produce more melanin and a, b and c less.

items: AABBCC (very dark) x aabbcc (very light) gives children all AaBbCc, of intermediate colour.
Two triple heterozygotes (AaBbCc x AaBbCc) give children from very dark to very light in the ratio 1 : 6 : 15 : 20 : 15 : 6 : 1.
AABBCC is the darkest (maximum melanin) and aabbcc the lightest (minimum melanin).

blocks.text: Wheat grain colour varies continuously from white to dark red and is controlled by three polygenes, A, B and C. Each dominant allele produces red pigment and each recessive allele does not, so AABBCC grains are dark red and aabbcc grains white. Dark red AABBCC x white aabbcc gives an F1 of intermediate red AaBbCc. In the F2 a wide range appears: one plant in 64 has the darkest red grains (AABBCC), one has white grains, and 62 show shades of red from moderate to very light.

blocks.alt: A bar chart of the F2 from AaBbCc x AaBbCc wheat. Seven bars, from 6 dominant alleles on the left to 0 on the right, have heights 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6 and 1, and are shaded from darkest red to white, with a grain of the same shade under each bar. The note says 1 of 64 is darkest red (AABBCC), 62 are in-between shades and 1 is white (aabbcc).
blocks.caption: Grain colour in the F2 of AaBbCc x AaBbCc wheat (original diagram after Figure 18.7).
blocks.long_description: Grain colour in wheat is controlled by three genes, A, B and C; each dominant allele adds red pigment and each recessive allele adds none, so the colour depends on how many dominant alleles a grain carries. Dark red AABBCC x white aabbcc gives an intermediate AaBbCc F1. Crossing two F1 plants gives 64 combinations, sorted by the number of dominant alleles from six to none in the ratio 1 : 6 : 15 : 20 : 15 : 6 : 1. The many small steps between darkest red and white make the variation continuous.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Environmental factors such as light, water and nutrients also influence grain colour.
